chunks: It is narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who sends a sacrificial animal voluntarily, and it is not obligatory.

He said: “He should arrange with his companions a day, and they should mark it. Then when that hour arrives, he avoids what the muhrim avoids until the Day of Sacrifice. Then when the Day of Sacrifice comes, it suffices for him.
For indeed, when the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was barred by the polytheists on the day of al-Ḥudaybiyyah, he slaughtered, exited ihram, and returned to al-Madīnah.”

key_terms.الْحُدَيْبِيَةِ: al-Ḥudaybiyyah, the historical location cited as precedent
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: the person in ihram who must avoid certain acts
key_terms.الْهَدْيِ: the sacrificial animal sent for offering
key_terms.فَيُقَلِّدُونَهُ: they mark it as a sacrificial animal
key_terms.يَوْمِ النَّحْرِ: the Day of Sacrifice when the animal is slaughtered

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on someone who sends a sacrificial animal voluntarily while remaining with his family?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for one who sends a sacrificial animal voluntarily without personally departing for hajj. From the agreed time of designation, he observes the restrictions of the muhrim until the Day of Sacrifice, and the Imam عليه السلام supports this ruling by citing the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم at al-Ḥudaybiyyah.
